records.text: Archived State Farm Stadium calendars showed no RV show scheduled for the weekend of Charlie Kirk's memorial.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I went back on Wayback Machine, ... saved screenshots. ... There was no RV show that was on the calendar for this Cardinal Stadium.

verification.notes: Independent AP reporting corroborates the substantive conclusion that the stadium was available on September 21, 2025, and searches found no RV-show listing for that weekend. However, the specific archived-calendar screenshots cited by Owens were not publicly retrievable, so the archival-inspection claim itself could not be directly authenticated.

sources.title: What to know about State Farm Stadium, the venue hosting Charlie Kirk's memorial service Sunday - Associated Press
sources.relevance: Independently corroborates that the stadium was available that weekend, though it does not authenticate Owens's archived screenshots.

records.text: Candace Owens said the Wayback Machine showed only one listing from Erika Kirk's corporate real-estate career.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And when we dig up the relic of what that, what she was doing in corporate real estate, all we can find on Wayback Machine is that she had one listing.

verification.notes: A public StreetEasy record identifies one Corcoran listing under Erika Frantzve, while Zillow currently reports zero sales/listings. This supports the existence of one discoverable listing, but the exhaustive claim that the Wayback Machine showed only one could not be reproduced from current search access.

records.text: The earliest Wayback Machine evidence that Proclaim Streetwear offered clothing for sale is January 16, 2021.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That's the earliest indication on Wayback Machine that clothing items were actually available for sale on the website.

verification.notes: A live search did not surface a stable Internet Archive capture index proving January 16, 2021 was the first snapshot with clothing for sale. Wayback coverage is incomplete and the earliest available capture would not necessarily prove first commercial availability.

sources.title: Internet Archive Help - Using the Wayback Machine
sources.relevance: Explains archive coverage limitations relevant to why an earliest capture does not prove earliest sale.

records.text: Owens said Wayback Machine showed Monster Lab as a splash page from May 3, 2024 through August 3, 2025, and said they thought September 12, 2025 might have been when the website went live.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Why is this about or around the Charlie Kirk assassination when this website went live? So I go on to Wayback Machine and we see that Monster Labs was not a website like somebody was just sitting on the domain name and then it just sort of said Monster Labs in the corner for all of 2024. ... You can show them, then. What, do you want to show the May 3rd, 2024? It stayed like this for beginning May 3rd, 2024, if you want to call this a splash page of sorts. It's just sitting there, and then it is not live. It is not live all the way through 2025. And then something very mysterious happens, because we know this website is live on September 15th. ... We see that it has been archived on September 12th. We think September 12th might have been when this website went live because on August 3rd, it's still the splash page. This is 2025. So on August 3rd, we still have a splash page.

records.text: Owens alleged that Monster Lab captures from September 12, 2025 onward had been wiped because they displayed only “loading”; she said her assumption was that the site went live September 12, or maybe September 10 without an archive, and attributed the missing captures to an attempt to hide the precise launch date.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: On September 12th, though, we've got some action, except, ladies and gentlemen, I'm not kidding. I've never seen this before ever on Wayback Machine. ... There are all of these captures from September 12, 2025, moving forward of this website, and it's been wiped. ... So people did capture the website, but all you can get is loading. ... Loading. You can't see what was captured, so you cannot confirm. You can see someone's captured on that date. ... It just tells us loading. We know for a fact on September 15th it was active. For Erika Kirk, my assumption, based on the details of what was just given to us, is that September 12th is when this website went live. ... That's my assumption. Two days after, maybe it's even September 10th, but nobody archived it. My assumption is that on September 12th, since that is the date that they are deciding if they're going to delete it moving forward because they didn't want us to have a precise idea of when it went live, suddenly this website goes forward and it is paying people to create effectively slop.

records.text: Owens alleged the inaccessible September 12 Wayback Machine captures were a cleaning up of tracks and said she thought the hidden material would be anti-Candace campaigns.

appearances.snippet: That feels significant. Who can help us figure out why Wayback Machine is suddenly malfunctioning, why we can't see what was up on September 12th? Where my techies at? ... And that's the first time I have ever seen that where there are archived days and it's just loading. ... Can't tell you anything. They don't want us to see what campaign was live on September 12th. That is a cleaning up of the tracks. ... I'm interested. I think it's going to be campaigns that are anti-Candace. Am I seeing myself too much in this?
